overall.line: Of the 5 approvals this concept needs: 1 not permitted (zoning and use), 2 further review (entertainment permit, building permit and change of use), 1 insufficient information (alcohol licence), 1 allowed (health permit).

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Bar adding place of entertainment use in NCD-CASTRO, same zoning district, 186 m away on 18th Street corridor. Use decision (CUA) approved 2012. Nearly identical concept: entertainment accessory to alcohol service.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning Commission approved a place of entertainment as an accessory use to an established bar in NCD-CASTRO. This shows the Commission has accepted the bar-plus-entertainment pairing in this district when the bar use is already established or authorized. Filed March 2012, decided June 2012 (105 days).

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Bar seeking extended hours at 465-469 Castro (57 m away), same NCD-CASTRO zoning, only denial found in the candidate set. Use decision (CUA) denied December 1994.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning Commission denied a CUA to extend operating hours for an existing bar on Castro Street itself. The only denial among the comparables signals that hour extensions—especially in a residential-adjacent NCD—face scrutiny. Filed September 1994, decided December 1994 (73 days to denial).

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Modification of prior CUA for live entertainment in a restaurant and bar at 4109-4111 18th Street (156 m away), NCD-CASTRO. Use decision approved with midnight closing condition for live entertainment.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Commission approved live entertainment until midnight in a full-service restaurant and bar, amending prior conditions. The midnight cap on entertainment hours was kept, showing the Commission limits late-night entertainment even when approving the use. Filed January 1998, decided April 1998 (77 days).

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA for live entertainment at 4109-4111 18th Street (156 m away), NCD-CASTRO, approved 1996. Use decision shows entertainment approval on same block cluster as 2012.0205C.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Commission approved live entertainment in the Castro NCD without extracted conditions in the record. The brief 66-day timeline (filed September 1996, decided December 1996) suggests a straightforward approval when the use fits the district character.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Bar expansion at 465-469 Castro (57 m away, same property that was later denied hour extension in 1994.517C), NCD-CASTRO. Use decision (CUA) approved July 1995.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Commission approved expanding an existing bar and adding a bed-and-breakfast on the second floor at 465-469 Castro. This approval one year after the hour-extension denial at the same address shows the Commission will approve bar expansion but guards hours of operation. Filed April 1995, decided July 1995 (92 days).

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Bar adding pool tables and live entertainment at 2367-2375 Market (97 m away), NCT-Upper Market zoning, approved 1992. Use decision shows entertainment added to existing bar in adjacent commercial district.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Commission approved adding live entertainment and pool tables to an existing bar in the Upper Market NCD, 97 m from the Castro Theatre. The 259-day timeline (filed March 1992, decided November 1992) reflects older procedures, but the approval confirms entertainment-in-bars is authorized in nearby NCDs when conditioned. Adjacent district pattern.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral approving place of entertainment permit for an existing bar at 4067 18th Street (149 m), NCD-CASTRO, under Planning Code Section 715.48 which waives CUA when bar has been in regular entertainment operation. Approved 2011.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a POE permit referral without requiring a new CUA under Section 715.48, which allows bars already operating entertainment to formalize it. This is an agency referral (one-day turnaround), not a use decision; it suggests a path for established venues but does not apply to a new bar use at 429 Castro.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms in writing that a path exists, form the legal entity, obtain the EIN, and register the business with the City.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization with the California Secretary of State ($70) and obtain the federal Employer Identification Number online from the IRS (same day, free). Then register the business with the SF Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number, required for all other City permits. Also file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the SF County Clerk if the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name, and publish the statement in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks.

timeline_cost.notes: No timeline or cost range is given because zoning does not permit the concept as described at this address: Planning Code Section 715 prohibits uses of 4,000 square feet or more in NCD-CASTRO, and the concept is 24,138 square feet. In addition, nighttime entertainment on the second story is not permitted under Section 715, yet the concept proposes to intensify the existing nonconforming nighttime entertainment use across two floors. If Planning confirms in writing that a variance, code interpretation, or redesign to under 4,000 square feet on the first story only would allow the use, the timeline to approval would be approximately 210 to 600 days and the government cost approximately $7,000 to $38,000. These figures assume approvals are granted; they are not times or costs to a denial or withdrawal. The size prohibition must be resolved in writing with Planning before any application is filed or any fee is paid.
timeline_cost.path: No approval path: zoning does not permit the concept as described at this address.
timeline_cost.verification_note: The record references Section 715 but does not contain the rule text showing size limits, nighttime entertainment restrictions, concept size, or timeline/cost figures.

status_definitions.allowed: Allowed: the cited records or code sections show this approval is available as of right, or already exists for this space, without a discretionary hearing.
status_definitions.further_review: Further review: the approval is obtainable only through a discretionary or multi-step review (a hearing, a referral, a licence investigation) whose result the records do not settle.
status_definitions.potential_blocker: Potential blocker: a cited rule, cap or record could stop this approval or force a change to the concept unless a specific condition is met.
status_definitions.not_permitted: Not permitted: a cited code section prohibits this use or approval at this address as the concept is described.
status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.verified: Verified: stated directly by a cited record or code section that applies to this exact address, parcel or zoning district.
confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.
confidence_definitions.needs_confirmation: Needs confirmation: plausible but not supported by a record in hand; confirm with the agency or document named.
confidence_definitions.professional_review_required: Professional review required: depends on plans, an inspection, or legal or design judgment that public records cannot supply.

records_summary: 429 Castro St is the historic Castro Theatre (City Landmark #100), currently operating as a movie theater with an accessory snack bar. The zoning district (NCD-CASTRO) treats a bar use on both the first and second stories as a conditional use, requiring Planning Commission authorization. The records show three prior applications at this address: two withdrawn telecommunications CUAs and one approved 2001 snack bar accessory use permit. The Castro Street corridor is exceptionally dense with bars and alcohol licenses—26 food/drink businesses and 19 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 feet, flagging undue concentration risk.
